JRI Recorder, on Saxophone

Jump Right In: The Instrumental Series (Recorder), Book One, section by section, taught on saxophone in concert B♭, E♭, C minor and G minor: rote songs, executive skills with the saxophone fingering for every new note, pattern instruction, home study.

Keys and how to use this

The recorder book works in G-DO, B♭-DO, G-LA and F-DO. Here the class plays saxophone in concert keys instead:

Recorder book Concert key on saxophone E♭ alto writes B♭ tenor writes
G-DO B♭-DO (B♭ major) G-DO C-DO
B♭-DO E♭-DO (E♭ major) C-DO F-DO
G-LA C-LA (C minor) A-LA D-LA
D-LA (Book Two) G-LA (G minor) E-LA A-LA
F-DO, C-DO not chosen yet

Each section keeps the book’s three parts: Part I the rote song, Part II executive skills and pattern instruction, Part III home study. Where the book introduces new notes, the activity shows the saxophone fingering for each (choose alto, tenor or baritone; the choice is remembered). This is a skeleton: the pattern sets, reading pages and songs are the site’s general ones for now, not the book’s own. Pages (📖) are the Teacher’s Guide’s printed pages.

Works Cited

Grunow, Richard F., Edwin E. Gordon, and Christopher D. Azzara. Jump Right In: The Instrumental Series. Teacher’s Guide for Recorder. Rev. ed., GIA Publications, 1999. 24 rote songs transcribed into the jri-recorder set of apps/tunes/tunes-object.js (melody and chords), from the piano-accompaniment pages (pp. 258–315). Tonal Patterns from Student Book Two (pp. 321–324; major, minor, Dorian and Mixolydian tonic, dominant and subdominant sets, the minor, Dorian and Mixolydian ones being the site’s 322a/b, 323a/b, 324a/b) and the Student Book One tonic and dominant lesson set (pp. 46–47), jri-recorder-tonal-* in apps/patterns/pattern-set.js with C as DO (or LA, RE, SO); Rhythm Patterns from Student Book Two (pp. 325–334), jri-recorder-rhythm-* in apps/rhythms/rhythm-pattern-object.js. Reproduced with permission. MLT Books (recorder on saxophone): the Book One lesson plans, Units 1–12, Sections A and B, summarized part by part with their pages (pp. 36–177).
